turn.asked: Why is 0.45 wrong?? The meter says 0.45
turn.reply:
Hey, I get why you're confused — the meter does show 0.45 A right now, so it's natural to think it stays the same. But the question is about *after* you open switch S. Let's look at what changes.

Right now, with S closed, both bulbs are on. Bulb A gets 0.30 A and bulb B gets some current too — together they add up to 0.45 A at the main meter.

What happens to bulb B's branch when you open switch S? That switch S is right there on bulb B's branch. When you open it, bulb B's path is cut off. So only bulb A stays connected to the cell.

Now, with just bulb A (5 Ω) across the 1.5 V cell, can you work out what the current would be? Use Ohm's law — you've got the voltage and resistance right there on the board.
